Dovish-leaning with balance: The 50 bp cut, “greater confidence” that inflation is moving sustainably to 2%, and “risks…roughly in balance” signal an easing tilt consistent with forward-looking inflation-forecast targeting and optimal policy in New Keynesian frameworks (Svensson and Woodford, 2005; New Keynesian Phillips Curve). Relative to Taylor-rule benchmarks (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler), slowing job gains and a modestly higher unemployment rate justify a less restrictive stance, in line with dual-mandate stabilization and Okun’s law trade-offs. The implementation moves (lower IORB to 4.9% and ON RRP to 4.8%) reinforce easier financial conditions, though the continued balance-sheet runoff (QT caps unchanged) partially offsets the dovish impulse, consistent with the literature that rate policy and balance-sheet policy operate as distinct levers. Net tone: moderately positive for risk assets and financial conditions, but tempered by ongoing QT and data-dependence.
